name: Oubangui Riverfront and Rapids
subtitle: The vital river artery facing Zongo (DRC), defining Bangui's geography, trade, and canoe transport.

facts.label: Boundary
facts.value: Natural frontier dividing Central African Republic and Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.label: Geographic feature
facts.value: Upstream rapids that historically halted European river steamboats

facts.label: Daily life
facts.value: Traditional wooden pirogues, sand extractors, and cross-border ferry traffic to Zongo

parts.text: The defining landscape and economic lifeline of Bangui, lining the northern shore of the great Ubangi (Oubangui) River, the principal right-bank tributary of the Congo River. Directly across the waters lies the town of Zongo in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Established where navigation was interrupted by swirling rocky rapids, the riverfront teems with fleets of hand-carved wooden pirogues, sand miners dredging building materials, and fishermen, forming an essential artery of commerce and transit connecting landlocked CAR to the wider Congo basin.

gaps: Hydrological depth variations and seasonal low-water river navigation reports are incomplete.
